result.title: Real Time Motion Detection in Video Inspired by Photonic Time Stretch
result.summary: Motion perception is fundamental to computer vision and physical AI, and plays a central role in robotics, autonomous vehicles, human-computer interaction, and video compression. Traditional approaches such as background subtraction, frame-differencing and optical flow algorithms often struggle in complex or dynamic scenes, typically sacrificing spatial resolution for computational tractability. Here we introduce MoViD (Motion estimation via Virtual dispersion and phase Detection), a physics-inspired algorithm grounded in the principles that govern photonic time stretch - a highly successful ultrafast realtime data acquisition platform. Drawing inspiration from the optical physics therein, MoViD treats video as a collection of optical time series waveforms associated with pixels. Motion of an object through a pixel broadens the time series spectrum and, after group delay dispersion, induces a temporal phase that exists only if there is motion. Spatiotemporal group delay dispersion templates, corresponding to dielectric functions, classify specific motion trajectories. Unlike conventional empirical phase-based motion-analysis pipelines that require narrow-band spatial channelization and pyramid reconstruction, the physics-based MoViD operates directly on the broadband video signal, vastly increasing its computational speed. The resulting algorithm achieves unprecedented performance in both motion characterization and motion magnification, providing full-resolution motion mapping in real time at nearly 200 frames per second at 4K resolution and 70 frames per second for 8K video - orders of magnitude faster than classical optical flow approaches or learning-based methods. Notably, such extreme performance enables real time motion analysis at ultrahigh resolution for motion detection and compensation in robotics and other autonomous devices.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 MoViD，借鉴光子时间拉伸原理，将视频视为各像素的光学时间序列波形，利用物体经过像素导致的光谱展宽与群延迟色散产生的运动相位来检测运动，并用色散模板区分运动轨迹，在 4K 下接近 200 fps 实现全分辨率实时运动刻画与运动放大。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作本身不涉及 latent 推理，但其免空间通道化、免降采样的全分辨率实时运动表征，可能作为向 VLM 提供细粒度运动证据的前端，可供核查其相位类信号与视觉细节保留、动态取证效率之间的联系。
